title: Popups, Context Menus and Modals
summary: Popups are small windows that appear on request and close when you click elsewhere - right-click menus, pickers, confirmations. This lesson explains ImGui's popup model (open by ID, draw every frame while open), context menus on items and windows, modal dialogs that block the rest of the interface, and the classic "unsaved changes" confirmation.
markdown:
## Opening and drawing are separate

A popup has an ID, like a widget. You **open** it once, in reaction to something, and you **draw** it every frame with `BeginPopup`, which returns `true` only while it is open:

```cpp-norun
if (ImGui::Button("Pick a stone")) ImGui::OpenPopup("stone picker");     // once, on click

if (ImGui::BeginPopup("stone picker"))                                     // every frame
{
    for (const char* s : { "Granite", "Basalt", "Slate" })
        if (ImGui::Selectable(s)) chosen = s;                              // a Selectable closes the popup
    ImGui::EndPopup();                                                     // only if BeginPopup returned true
}
```

The popup closes by itself when the user clicks outside it, presses Escape, or clicks a `Selectable`/`MenuItem` inside it. Close it from code with `ImGui::CloseCurrentPopup()` inside the popup.

Both calls must be made with the **same ID stack**: an `OpenPopup` inside a `PushID(i)` opens a popup that `BeginPopup` can only find inside the same `PushID(i)`. This is the most common popup bug, and a direct consequence of lesson 1.05.

## Context menus

Right-click menus have shortcuts that do the opening for you:

```cpp-norun
ImGui::Selectable(stone.name.c_str());
if (ImGui::BeginPopupContextItem())                   // right-click on the item just drawn
{
    if (ImGui::MenuItem("Rename")) startRename(stone);
    if (ImGui::MenuItem("Delete")) deleteStone(stone);
    ImGui::EndPopup();
}

if (ImGui::BeginPopupContextWindow(nullptr, ImGuiPopupFlags_MouseButtonRight | ImGuiPopupFlags_NoOpenOverItems))
{                                                      // right-click on empty space in the window
    if (ImGui::MenuItem("Add stone")) addStone();
    ImGui::EndPopup();
}
```

## Modals

A **modal** popup blocks interaction with everything behind it until it is closed, and dims the background. Use it for decisions that must be made before continuing:

```cpp-norun
if (wantsToQuit && level.dirty) ImGui::OpenPopup("Unsaved changes");

ImGui::SetNextWindowPos(ImGui::GetMainViewport()->GetCenter(), ImGuiCond_Appearing, ImVec2(0.5f, 0.5f));
if (ImGui::BeginPopupModal("Unsaved changes", nullptr, ImGuiWindowFlags_AlwaysAutoResize))
{
    ImGui::Text("Save changes to %s before quitting?", level.name.c_str());
    if (ImGui::Button("Save", ImVec2(100, 0)))       { save(); quit(); ImGui::CloseCurrentPopup(); }
    ImGui::SameLine();
    if (ImGui::Button("Don't save", ImVec2(100, 0))) { quit(); ImGui::CloseCurrentPopup(); }
    ImGui::SameLine();
    if (ImGui::Button("Cancel", ImVec2(100, 0)))     { wantsToQuit = false; ImGui::CloseCurrentPopup(); }
    ImGui::EndPopup();
}
```

`SetNextWindowPos` with the pivot `(0.5, 0.5)` and `ImGuiCond_Appearing` centres the dialog each time it appears. Passing a `bool*` as the second argument gives the modal a close button.

## The unsaved-changes flow

"Quit", "New level" and "Open level" all have the same shape: if there are unsaved changes, ask first; then do the action only if the user saved or chose not to. A small state machine keeps it correct: remember the **pending action**, open the modal, and when a button is pressed run (or drop) the pending action. The practice builds it.

## Common mistakes

> [!warning] OpenPopup and BeginPopup under different ID stacks
> The popup is opened but never found. Call both at the same PushID level.

> [!warning] Calling OpenPopup every frame
> The popup reopens and resets constantly. Open it once, in response to an event.

> [!warning] Using a modal for information
> Modals interrupt. Use them for decisions only; show information in a tooltip or a log.

## Check yourself
```quiz
? Describe ImGui's popup model.
- You call OpenPopup every frame while the popup should be visible, and BeginPopup draws it
+ A popup has an ID; OpenPopup marks it open once, and BeginPopup, called every frame, returns true and draws it while it is open
- BeginPopup opens the popup and keeps it open until you call EndPopup
- A popup is a separate window you create once and destroy with CloseCurrentPopup
> Opening is an event, drawing happens every frame. The popup closes on outside clicks, Escape, a Selectable or MenuItem inside it, or CloseCurrentPopup.

? What do BeginPopupContextItem and BeginPopupContextWindow do?
- They open a popup when the item or window is hovered, then wait for a click inside it
- They draw a tooltip next to the item or the window
+ They open and begin a popup when the item just drawn, or empty space in the window, is right-clicked
> They do the OpenPopup call for you on a right-click, then work like BeginPopup, so EndPopup still goes inside the if.

? How do you centre a modal each time it appears?
- SetNextWindowPos at the viewport's centre with ImGuiCond_Always and the default pivot
- SetNextWindowPos at the viewport's centre with ImGuiCond_Once
- Pass ImGuiWindowFlags_AlwaysAutoResize to BeginPopupModal
+ SetNextWindowPos at the main viewport's centre, with pivot (0.5, 0.5) and ImGuiCond_Appearing
> The pivot puts the window's middle, not its corner, on the point, and ImGuiCond_Appearing applies it each time it opens while still letting the user move it.

? How often do you call OpenPopup and BeginPopup?
- Both every frame
+ OpenPopup once when it should open; BeginPopup every frame
- Both once, when the popup should open
> Calling OpenPopup every frame keeps reopening and resetting the popup; BeginPopup must run every frame to draw it.

? OpenPopup("menu") is called inside PushID(3), BeginPopup("menu") outside it. What happens?
- It works normally, because both use the label "menu"
- ImGui opens two popups
+ The popup never appears, because the IDs differ
> Popup IDs follow the ID stack, so both calls must be made at the same PushID level.

? When should you use a modal popup?
- For every message the user should read, such as a log line
- For hints shown when the mouse rests on a widget
+ For a decision needed before continuing, such as unsaved changes
> Modals block everything else until answered. Information belongs in a tooltip or a log.
```
